sources.entry: selenium - Python bindings for Selenium WebDriver.

summary.one_liner: Selenium is an umbrella browser-automation project whose README is a developer guide for building, testing, and contributing to its multi-language WebDriver bindings.
summary.what_it_does: The README covers the contributor workflow for the Selenium monorepo, which provides infrastructure for the W3C WebDriver specification across Java, Python, Ruby, C#, JavaScript and Rust. It explains setting up a dev environment on macOS, Windows and Linux, including Bazelisk, a JDK 17+, and optional Dev Container or Docker setups. It documents the Bazel-based build (with a ./go Rake wrapper) and per-language local install steps, such as building the Python package from source. It also describes test filtering by size and tag, running browser tests under a virtual X server, and the documentation and release commands. It does not describe end-user usage; it points to a separate User Manual for that.
use_cases: set up a local Selenium development environment
run Selenium browser tests headless or under Xvfb
contribute a pull request to Selenium
install Selenium Python package from source
how_to_run: Install Bazelisk and a Java JDK 17 or greater, setting JAVA_HOME
Build everything for a language: bazel build //... (see README for exact target pattern)
./go py:local_dev to generate files for running Python from source
bazel test //... --test_size_filters=small to run unit tests
notable: Single monorepo covering several language bindings built with one Bazel build system
Bazel output-base and cache guidance for working across multiple git worktrees
Test filtering by size (small, medium, large) and by tag
Selenium Manager can be compiled from source or stubbed for tests
Ships a Windows dev-environment setup script
caveats: Windows setup is involved, requiring MSYS2, Visual Studio C++ tools, and long-path registry changes
The README says the Windows setup article it links to is out of date
Local development requires a Bazel toolchain and Java JDK even for the Python bindings
